name: Cinemas and theatres

problems.words: Box office cash doesn't match ticket counts
quick_ideas: Count cash with the next shift at handover, so a gap belongs to one shift
Match one day's tickets against cash and card per cashier, to see where gaps start.

workzap_build.text: a daily box-office reconciliation by show and cashier, flagging gaps to the owner automatically.

problems.ask_first: Do you sell only at the counter or through apps too?
problems.free_stops: How ticketing data is pulled in and matched is in the solution document.

problems.words: Online ticket app numbers and our counter numbers never reconcile
quick_ideas: Compare one week of app sales with your own records by show, to see which shows differ
Note which app's settlement doesn't match what you expected, since that is where to start.

workzap_build.text: a reconciliation view matching counter, app and cash or card totals every day.

problems.ask_first: How many ticketing apps sell your seats?
problems.free_stops: The data connection and matching rules stay for the solution document.

problems.words: Complimentary tickets are given out too freely
quick_ideas: Decide who may give a free ticket and why, so comps stop being casual
Check last week's comps once by staff member, to see whether one name stands out.

workzap_build.text: a comp and refund approval flow with reasons logged and totals in the morning read.

problems.ask_first: Who can give a free ticket today?
problems.free_stops: Approval levels and reasons list go in the solution document.

problems.words: Popcorn and drinks stock doesn't match sales
quick_ideas: Count drinks and key items at every shift change for a week, to see which shift loses stock
Make one person sign for the candy bar each shift, so stock has an owner.

workzap_build.text: a concession tracker with opening and closing counts per shift compared to sales, with mismatches and wastage flagged.

problems.free_stops: Count routine and wastage logging are designed in the solution document.

problems.words: Popcorn and hot food thrown away every night
quick_ideas: Note what's thrown out each night for a week, to see which days you over-make
Prepare in smaller batches for quiet shows, since a weekday matinee doesn't need a weekend batch.

workzap_build.text: a wastage log tied to show occupancy, showing which days and shows waste most.

problems.free_stops: How preparation is linked to bookings is in the solution document.

problems.words: Weekday afternoon shows run nearly empty
quick_ideas: Look at which weekday shows are weakest, since fewer shows can mean fuller halls
Think of one group, such as students or families, who could fill daytime shows, because they need a different invitation.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp updates to regulars who agreed to hear from you, about weekday shows and offers.

problems.ask_first: How many screens do you run?
problems.free_stops: Which audiences to target and when are planned in the solution document.

problems.words: Projector or sound breaks during a show
quick_ideas: Write down every failure this month with date and cause, to see what keeps breaking
Agree with your technician what is checked before the first show, so problems surface before the audience sits.

workzap_build.text: an equipment log for projectors and sound with downtime recorded and service reminders.

problems.ask_first: Is your technician on staff or on call?
problems.free_stops: Equipment list and service schedule stay for the solution document.

problems.words: Distributor settlement statements take days by hand
quick_ideas: Use one statement layout for every film and distributor, so you stop rebuilding it
Record ticket sales per film weekly, so settlement isn't a scramble.

workzap_build.text: settlement statements generated automatically per film per week from ticket sales.

problems.ask_first: How many distributors do you settle with?
problems.free_stops: Statement content and data sources go in the solution document.

problems.words: Customers call asking showtimes all day
quick_ideas: Post the week's showtimes in one place and point every caller to it, so the phone stops ringing for the same thing
Make one person responsible for keeping it right, since wrong times cause the angriest calls.

workzap_build.text: a WhatsApp showtime assistant answering "what's on tonight" from the live schedule.

problems.ask_first: Is your website showtime list kept up to date?
problems.free_stops: The assistant's answers and schedule connection are in the solution document.

problems.words: I can't compare our two locations properly
quick_ideas: Agree the same few numbers from each location daily, so you compare like with like
Put one week side by side, to see which location needs attention.

workzap_build.text: a morning read per location with tickets, occupancy, concessions, comps and refunds.

problems.ask_first: Do both locations use the same ticketing system?
problems.free_stops: Which numbers and how they're pulled is in the solution document.

never_say: Advice on censorship, content approvals, distribution contracts or entertainment tax. Help with piracy, unlicensed screenings or hiding ticket sales. Fire codes or crowd safety guidance; fire, crush or medical emergency means emergency services immediately. Collecting audience names, contacts or card details.

sample_reply.person: Candy bar ka maal sales se match nahi karta, khaas taur pe drinks gayab hote hain. Koi hal batayein.
sample_reply.pi: Ji, is par jald qaboo paya ja sakta hai. 1 Ek hafte tak har shift badalne par drinks aur khaas items gine jayein, taake pata chale kis shift mein farq aata hai. 2 Har shift mein ek banda candy bar ke stock ka zimmedar ho. Workzap yeh aap ke liye khud-ba-khud kar sakta hai: har shift ki ginti sales se mila kar farq foran aap tak pohanche. Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
